findings.quote: Delighted at first, he promised everything; but then, in some distrust, he examined in detail the several plans and preparations.
findings.problem: τὰ μὲν ὑπερχαρὴς ὢν πάνθ᾽ ὑπισχνεῖτο, τὰ δὲ διαπιστῶν ἐξήταζε: τὰ μὲν ... τὰ δὲ means 'in part ... in part', two simultaneous attitudes, not a sequence 'at first ... but then'. The true sequence comes only with μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα πιστεύσας in the next sentence.
findings.proposed_fix: Partly overjoyed, he promised everything; partly distrustful, he examined in detail the several plans and preparations.

findings.quote: afterward to make his move, by a circuitous route, toward Syria
findings.problem: μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ποιήσασθαι δίχα προόδου τὴν ὁρμὴν ἐπὶ τοὺς κατὰ Συρίαν τόπους: δίχα προόδου is 'without any preliminary advance' (a sudden dash); nothing in the Greek says 'circuitous route'.
findings.proposed_fix: afterward to make his dash, without any preliminary advance, for the regions of Syria

findings.quote: led him by the same route by which he had come, and brought him alone before Antiochus
findings.problem: ᾗ μὲν ἦλθε νυκτί, ταύτῃ παράγει πρὸς τὸν Ἀντίοχον τὸν Βῶλιν ὁ Καμβύλος μόνος πρὸς μόνον: ᾗ ... νυκτί is dative of time, 'on the night on which he came, on that same night'; there is no 'route'. μόνος πρὸς μόνον: Cambylus, alone, to the king, alone (private audience).
findings.proposed_fix: brought him, on that same night, to Antiochus, in private, with no one else present

findings.quote: the task would be difficult for those in whom he trusted
findings.problem: δύσχρηστος ἡ πρόθεσις ἀπέβαινε τοῖς πεπιστευμένοις: οἱ πεπιστευμένοι are those entrusted with the task (Bolis and Cambylus), not men in whom Achaeus (or anyone) put trust; 'he' invites misreading as Achaeus.
findings.proposed_fix: the task would be difficult for those entrusted with it

findings.quote: some joining Ariobazus and others Laodice
findings.problem: Greek reads οἱ μὲν πρὸς Ἀρίβαζον: the name is Aribazus (Ἀρίβαζος), not Ariobazus/Ariobarzanes.
findings.proposed_fix: some joining Aribazus and others Laodice

units.note: The Greek ends with an apparatus note: a one-folio lacuna follows (post unius folii lacunam v. VIII, 36, 9). The chapter itself is complete as transmitted; the seam is an apparatus matter, not a smoothing inside the English.
English omits the testimonium frame 'Polybius, in the eighth book of the Histories, says ...' (Athenaeus) but this is not within the error classes.

Mithridates, 'son of his sister' (υἱὸς τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτοῦ): αὐτοῦ is ambiguous in the Greek (Antiochus's or Xerxes's sister); the English 'his' preserves the ambiguity. Numbers 300 talents, 1000 horses, 1000 mules correct.
